name: Satyapan Forensic Lab investigation dataset v1

scenario.title: Operation Pratibimb — 'digital arrest' extortion of a retired professor
scenario.summary: On 21-10-2026 the complainant, a 68-year-old retired professor (fictional), received a WhatsApp video call from a man posing as an enquiry officer, a 'notice' threatening arrest, an 'officer ID' photo, and voice notes in his daughter's voice and in Hindi pleading for money. He transferred ₹4,50,000. The exhibits below were extracted from his phone and the suspect's seized laptop and sent for authentication, deepfake detection and source attribution.

items.description: Screen recording of the WhatsApp video call with the 'enquiry officer'.
items.how_made: Real phone video with an AI-generated face overlaid by an online face-swap service (UniData sample deepfake/1.mp4).
items.license: UniData deepfake-videos-dataset sample, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (consented; copied unmodified)

items.description: Video clip recovered from the suspect's laptop.
items.how_made: The genuine phone recording the deepfake was made from (UniData video/1.mp4).
items.license: UniData deepfake-videos-dataset sample, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (consented; copied unmodified)

items.description: Profile photo found on a social-media account used by the suspects.
items.how_made: The face image used for the swap (UniData image/1.jpg).
items.license: UniData deepfake-videos-dataset sample, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (consented; copied unmodified)

items.description: Known voice sample of the complainant's daughter (control sample for speaker comparison).
items.how_made: Genuine human speech: LJSpeech public-domain recordings LJ001-0001..0004.

items.description: Voice note that appears to be from the complainant's daughter.
items.how_made: Piper TTS voice en_US-ljspeech-high (a neural TTS trained on the same speaker as the known sample, i.e. a voice clone), encoded as a WhatsApp-style Opus voice note.
items.license: Generated for this dataset (Piper MIT; LJSpeech public domain)

items.description: Hindi voice note from the 'CBI officer' announcing a 'digital arrest'.
items.how_made: Piper TTS voice hi_IN-rohan-medium (synthetic Hindi speech), WhatsApp-style Opus.

items.description: Recording of a phone call offered as proof that the complainant agreed to 'invest'.
items.how_made: Genuine human speech (LJSpeech) from two recording sessions with different mains-hum frequencies and background noise, joined at 16.54 s.
items.license: Generated for this dataset (LJSpeech public domain)

items.description: Blank notice template recovered from the suspect's laptop.
items.how_made: Rendered for this dataset (fictional agency), saved once at JPEG quality 92.

items.description: 'Notice of preliminary enquiry' sent to the complainant.
items.how_made: The template with the addressee and amount pasted in from a separately compressed render (splice) and the round stamp lifted and cloned onto the left of the page (copy-move); resized to 1600 px and re-compressed like a WhatsApp image.

items.description: 'Officer ID card' photo, original file sent on Telegram.
items.how_made: SD-Turbo text-to-image (2 steps), signed C2PA manifest declaring trainedAlgorithmicMedia (test CA, not on a trust list). Stability's reference invisible watermark was applied, but on this flat-background portrait neither the reference decoder nor Satyapan's can read it back: watermarks are fragile.

truth_detail.prompt: passport style studio portrait photograph of a stern middle-aged Indian man in a khaki police uniform, plain light grey background, sharp focus, 50mm photo
truth_detail.c2pa: c2pa.created / trainedAlgorithmicMedia, signed by a throw-away demo CA

items.description: Same 'officer' photo as received on WhatsApp.
items.how_made: The SD-Turbo portrait cropped, resized to 400 px and re-compressed (watermark and Content Credentials lost).

notes: Ground truth for every exhibit. The scenario and its people are fictional. Media of real people come only from public research datasets: UniData's consented participants (the face swap is UniData's own sample) and LJSpeech (public domain); the 'daughter' voice note uses the public Piper voice trained on LJSpeech. These media are built locally by `make demo-dataset` and are never committed (AGENTS.md data hygiene).
